title: High-throughput Imaging for Everyone: New Designs for Parallel Multiwell Imaging
content: Many life-science experiments require capturing images from different samples in multiwell plates. Most use robotics to move the microscope field of view to sequentially sample each well, generating a series of short measurements. Some assays, however, require continuous long-duration recordings: slowly evolving processes (metastasis, organoid or embryo development), unpredictable dynamical event (cardiac transitions to arrhythmia), and behavioral studies in model organisms (zebrafish, C Elegans) must be imaged in parallel if replicates are required. Continuous measurements in many samples have been achieved by using a wide-field lens or using many detectors[1-3], however these approaches greatly reduce spatial resolution or increase system cost.
